title: Hosting decision — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a teammate asks why the service is not containerized. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud, in under a minute, which hosting model you picked and name the one condition that would make you revisit it.

vocabulary.meaning: the runtime model a service is deployed on, chosen for its operational cost rather than its popularity
the future fact that would make you revisit a decision, stated when the decision is taken rather than after

expectedElements: The hosting model is named, not described vaguely
The reason is operational cost, not preference
One condition that would reverse the choice
modelAnswer: We run it on a managed application platform rather than in a container. The reason is operational: we do not maintain a base image, and platform updates are not our work. My evidence is the deployment definition plus the health endpoint answering after a restart. The limitation is that we cannot shift a fraction of traffic to a new revision, so a risky release has to go out whole. If weighted rollout becomes a requirement, that single fact reverses the choice. Does anything in the roadmap need traffic splitting in the next quarter?
commonMistakes: Defending the platform on popularity instead of on the maintenance it removes
Presenting the choice as permanent, with no condition that would reverse it
variants: Answer again assuming the team has just been asked to run a canary release next month.
